items.claim: logProviderCompareMethod reports the compare method using GetEnvOrFile + EqualFold, but every provider passes raw os.Getenv(<X>_COMPARE) to githosts, which validates case-sensitively, so the startup log can contradict what actually runs.
items.consequence: GITHUB_COMPARE=REFS: startup logs 'GitHub compare method: refs', then NewGitHubHost rejects it with 'invalid diff remote method: REFS' and the GitHub backup fails. GITHUB_COMPARE_FILE=/run/secrets/cmp containing 'refs': startup logs 'refs' but the provider gets '' and silently uses clone. Carried over from the old code, now centralised for all five providers.

items.claim: checkProvidersDefined special-cases both BitBucket providers and never routes them to checkProvider, so a partial BitBucket configuration is silently ignored.
items.consequence: BITBUCKET_EMAIL set, BITBUCKET_API_TOKEN missing or misspelled, GITHUB_TOKEN set: validation passes with no 'parameter is not defined' error, displayBitBucketStartupConfig still logs BitBucket settings, and collectProviderBackupResults skips BitBucket without any log. BitBucket repos are never backed up and the run reports success.

items.claim: checkJustTokenProvider counts non-empty auth parameters, including API URLs, rather than configured providers, so a provider with only its URL set counts as defined even though it will never run.
items.consequence: Only GITEA_APIURL (or SOURCEHUT_APIURL) set, no token: count is 1, so 'no providers defined' is not raised. collectProviderBackupResults gates on GITEA_TOKEN and runs nothing; the run logs 'all backups failed', sends a failed notification, and exits 0. checkProvider's doc comment also still says it returns 0 or 1, while Gitea with both set returns 2.

items.claim: validateStartupConfig reads GIT_BACKUP_DIR with os.LookupEnv and returns a newline-trimmed value, but scheduleBackups ignores that value and runProviderBackups re-reads the raw setting via GetEnvOrFile.
items.consequence: GIT_BACKUP_DIR_FILE=/run/secrets/dir with no GIT_BACKUP_DIR: displayStartupConfig logs 'root backup directory: /data', then Run aborts with 'environment variable GIT_BACKUP_DIR must be set'. With a trailing newline in GIT_BACKUP_DIR, the stat and working dir use the trimmed path while backups and cleanup use the untrimmed one.

items.claim: displayBitBucketStartupConfig gates only on BITBUCKET_EMAIL instead of the new bitbucketAPITokenDefined() || bitbucketOAuthDefined() helpers that decide whether BitBucket actually runs.
items.consequence: OAuth2-only setup (BITBUCKET_USER/KEY/SECRET): BitBucket is backed up but its retention, compare method and LFS settings are never logged at startup. Email-only incomplete setup: the settings are logged although BitBucket will not run. Sourcehut has no startup display at all.

items.claim: scheduleBackups creates a gocron scheduler unconditionally, including on the one-shot path where it is never started or shut down, and it is also not shut down when NewJob fails.
items.consequence: With neither GIT_BACKUP_INTERVAL nor GIT_BACKUP_CRON set, every run allocates a scheduler that is never used or released; an invalid cron expression returns 'failed to create job' and leaves the scheduler behind. Moving NewScheduler into the new runScheduledJob (with Shutdown on error) would remove both.

items.claim: The new bitbucketAPITokenDefined/bitbucketOAuthDefined helpers remove two copies of the credential-completeness check, but Bitbucket() in internal/bitbucket.go lines 15-25 still has its own copy.
items.consequence: A later change to what counts as complete (for example trimming whitespace, as checkProvider does) made in the helpers would let validation and scheduling disagree with Bitbucket(), which would then return 'BitBucket authentication not properly configured' or pick the wrong auth type.

items.claim: titleBackupsErrors and titleBackupsFailed start with a stray invisible U+FE0F variation selector (bytes EF B8 8F) before the emoji, copied verbatim from the old literals into the shared constants.
items.consequence: Every 'completed with errors' or 'failed' notification sends a title starting with an orphan variation selector in the ntfy Title header, Slack text and Telegram text. Clients can render a blank or tofu glyph, and filters matching on a title starting with the emoji never match; the success title has no such prefix.

items.claim: The rewritten RUN keeps `rm -f "/var/cache/apk/*"`, where the quoted glob never expands, alongside `--update` combined with `--no-cache`.
items.consequence: The rm targets a literal file named '*' and does nothing, so the cleanup step is dead and misleading; it is also redundant because --no-cache already leaves no cache. The line was edited for Sonar findings but the no-op remains.

items.claim: The refactored TestGiteaOrgsRepositoryBackup still calls resetBackups() in each switch arm and again right after the switch, and the two new assert helpers duplicate the org-two assertions.
items.consequence: Each iteration wipes the backup directory twice in a row, with a third wipe from the deferred call at the end. The org-two DirExists/ReadDir/Len/prefix checks exist in both assertGiteaOrgTwoOnlyBackedUp and assertGiteaAllOrgsBackedUp, so a fixture change must be made in two places.
